albums.blurb: Glass wrote Glassworks in 1981 as his first studio album for CBS, deliberately scaling his style down from the operas Einstein on the Beach and Satyagraha into six short chamber movements — Opening, Floe, Islands, Rubric, Façades, Closing — conceived for home listening on the then-new Walkman. The Philip Glass Ensemble under Michael Riesman plays an entirely instrumental lineup of piano, flutes, saxophones, horns, low strings and synthesizer, and the record was among the first by a living composer to be recorded digitally.
albums.reception: It became and remains Glass's best-selling record of his middle period, the album through which much of his audience first encountered his music.

albums.blurb: Jockstrap is the London duo of Georgia Ellery — also the violinist of Black Country, New Road — and producer Taylor Skye, who met as students at the Guildhall School of Music & Drama. I Love You Jennifer B, their debut full-length for Rough Trade after a run of EPs including Wicked City, sets Ellery's torch-song melodies and strings against Skye's volatile electronics, lurching between chamber ballad and club music inside single tracks.
albums.reception: The album was shortlisted for the 2023 Mercury Prize.

albums.blurb: Baker was the poster boy of West Coast cool jazz, a trumpeter who broke out in Gerry Mulligan's pianoless quartet before leading his own groups. Chet Baker Sings, cut for Pacific Jazz in 1954 with pianist Russ Freeman and expanded to its familiar fourteen-track form in 1956, was his first full album as a vocalist — producer Dick Bock indulged the idea skeptically, and the hushed, nearly vibratoless singing on songs like My Funny Valentine ended up defining Baker's public image as much as his horn did.
albums.reception: Readers' polls in the jazz press of the day voted Baker the top jazz vocalist, and the album was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2001.
